SAF-INDUCTIVE-ON-PIN.title: {part} is wired straight to pin {pin}
SAF-INDUCTIVE-ON-PIN.why: A motor needs far more current than an Arduino pin can give (40 mA absolute maximum), and its voltage spikes can destroy the pin.
SAF-INDUCTIVE-ON-PIN.fix: Drive the motor through a motor driver such as the L298N, or a transistor with a flyback diode.

SAF-LED-NO-RESISTOR.title: {part} has no current-limiting resistor
SAF-LED-NO-RESISTOR.why: Without a resistor the LED draws far more than its 20 mA rating and burns out — and it can damage the pin driving it.
SAF-LED-NO-RESISTOR.fix: Put a 220 Ω – 1 kΩ resistor in series with the LED.

SAF-SHORT-CIRCUIT.title: {part} is short-circuited
SAF-SHORT-CIRCUIT.why: Its + and − are joined with almost no resistance: it heats up, drains at once and can melt wires.
SAF-SHORT-CIRCUIT.fix: Remove the direct connection between + and −.

SAF-OVERVOLTAGE.title: {part} gets {volts, number} V (maximum {max, number} V)
SAF-OVERVOLTAGE.why: Above its absolute maximum voltage a part is damaged immediately.
SAF-OVERVOLTAGE.fix: Use a lower supply voltage or add a regulator.

SAF-REVERSE-POLARITY.title: {part} is powered backwards
SAF-REVERSE-POLARITY.why: Reversed supply polarity destroys most electronic parts.

SAF-PIN-CURRENT.title: Pin {pin} carries {ma, number} mA (limit {limit, number} mA)
SAF-PIN-CURRENT.why: Each ATmega328P pin is rated 20 mA; 40 mA is the absolute maximum before the pin is damaged.
SAF-PIN-CURRENT.fix: Add or increase the series resistor, or switch the load with a transistor or driver.

SAF-MCU-TOTAL-CURRENT.title: The Arduino would supply {ma, number} mA in total (limit {limit, number} mA)
SAF-MCU-TOTAL-CURRENT.why: All I/O pins together share the chip's power pins, which carry only about 200 mA.
SAF-MCU-TOTAL-CURRENT.fix: Power the loads from a separate supply through transistors or drivers.

SAF-SUPPLY-OVERLOAD.title: {supply} gives at most {limit, number} mA, but its loads can draw {ma, number} mA
SAF-SUPPLY-OVERLOAD.why: When motors or servos stall, the supply voltage collapses and the board resets or the regulator overheats.
SAF-SUPPLY-OVERLOAD.fix: Give the motors or servos their own stronger supply and connect its − to GND.

SAF-FLOATING-INPUT.title: Pin {pin} is a floating input
SAF-FLOATING-INPUT.why: With nothing pulling it HIGH or LOW, the pin reads random noise.
SAF-FLOATING-INPUT.fix: Use pinMode(…, INPUT_PULLUP) or add a 10 kΩ pull-up or pull-down resistor.

SAF-NO-COMMON-GROUND.title: {part}'s − is not connected to the common ground
SAF-NO-COMMON-GROUND.why: Signals between two circuits only work when their grounds are joined.
SAF-NO-COMMON-GROUND.fix: Connect the − of {part} to Arduino GND.

SAF-BACKFEED.title: Two supplies drive the same rail: {parts}
SAF-BACKFEED.why: Supplies fighting each other back-feed regulators and the USB port.
SAF-BACKFEED.fix: Keep a single source on each rail — for example, remove the L298N regulator jumper.

SAF-OUTPUTS-FIGHTING.title: Outputs {pins} are wired together and fighting
SAF-OUTPUTS-FIGHTING.why: One pin drives HIGH while the other drives LOW: a short circuit straight through both pins.
SAF-OUTPUTS-FIGHTING.fix: Never connect two outputs; use one pin, or put a resistor between them.

SAF-COMPONENT-FAULT.title: {part} was damaged ({code})
SAF-COMPONENT-FAULT.why: It ran outside its ratings long enough to fail.
SAF-COMPONENT-FAULT.fix: Fix the wiring fault, then reset the simulation.

SAF-LOGIC-OSCILLATION.title: Logic outputs keep changing and never settle
SAF-LOGIC-OSCILLATION.why: Gates are wired in a loop that feeds an output back to an input of opposite sense, so the circuit oscillates instead of holding a value.
SAF-LOGIC-OSCILLATION.fix: Break the feedback loop, or add a clock or latch where you meant to store a value.
